title: Xinran Zhou
text: INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH Xinran Zhou Environmental economics · Ecosystem science · Geospatial analysis I use quantitative methods to examine environmental and economic questions in agriculture, ecosystems, and land management. Email LinkedIn ABOUT ME Background and research interests I am completing a Professional Science Master’s in Ecosystem Science & Sustainability (Carbon Management) at Colorado State University, while pursuing an M.S. in Population, Resources & Environmental Economics at Shandong University. I earned a B.A. in Economics from China University of Geosciences (Wuhan). My experience spans life cycle assessment and costing, ecosystem modeling workflows, geospatial analysis, and quantitative economics—including panel-data econometrics, evolutionary game modeling, and agricultural input–output data analysis. I am interested in the economic feasibility and environmental trade-offs of agricultural and land-management decisions across different landscapes. title: Research and Technical Experience
text: Research and Technical Experience Selected Research Environmental and economic assessment of synthetic humic substances This research at Shandong University evaluates four synthetic humic substance production pathways and their agricultural applications in China. A regionalized LCA-LCC framework compares environmental impacts, production costs, and monetized environmental externalities across crop systems, regions, and electricity scenarios. View portfolio Forest cover change across Colorado’s Front Range, 2001–2021 Collaborative research at CU Boulder’s Environmental Data Science Innovation and Impact Lab (ESIIL) examines forest-cover change across Colorado’s Front Range. Python and Google Earth Engine workflows combine land-cover, elevation, and burned-area data to analyze land-cover transitions and spatial patterns of forest loss. View portfolio Wind power policy and corporate sustainability This study examines how wind-power policy instruments relate to corporate sustainability using panel data from 58 listed firms between 2009 and 2021. Two-way fixed-effects models are complemented by mechanism, robustness, and heterogeneity analyses across ownership types and regions. Renewable Portfolio Standards A tripartite evolutionary game model examines interactions among government, renewable-energy producers, and consumers under Renewable Portfolio Standards. MATLAB simulations and sensitivity analyses explore how certificate prices, penalties, and transaction costs affect stakeholder strategies. Model Testing and Data Work MEMS Grazing Scheduler testing Technical work at LandEngine, Colorado State University, focuses on testing the MEMS Grazing Scheduler with site-specific inputs and continuous, low-rotation, and adaptive multi-paddock grazing scenarios. Tasks include model setup, test runs, troubleshooting, output checks, and workflow documentation. View portfolio China-specific FABIO framework Work on a China-specific Food and Agriculture Biomass Input-Output (FABIO) framework harmonizes agricultural, biomass, economic, and environmental data. Product-level flow accounts, mappings for 84 agricultural products, and environmental satellite accounts connect agricultural flows with environmental pressures.

title: Research Portfolio
text: SELECTED WORK & RESEARCH COMMUNICATION Research portfolio A curated look at real research questions, datasets, and analytical approaches. This page replaces the earlier illustrative sample charts with descriptions grounded in completed or ongoing projects. REMOTE SENSING & SPATIAL DATA 01 / Colorado Front Range forest change Data: NLCD land-cover maps for 2001 and 2021, burned-area datasets, and elevation models. Analysis: land-cover transitions, forest-type change, spatial overlap with burned areas, and elevation-related patterns using Python and Google Earth Engine. ~19% decrease in mapped forest cover in the team’s 2001–2021 study; an association, not a causal estimate Collaborative work through ESIIL. The presentation includes team and mentor contributions. Research figures and slide files are not republished here pending sharing review. Read the project summary ENVIRONMENTAL–ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT 02 / Synthetic humic substances for agricultural applications System: four crop-residue-derived production pathways and modeled applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple systems in China. Assessment: life cycle impacts, internal production costs, monetized environmental externalities, crop-specific substitution scenarios, and regional electricity mixes. Interpretation: results depend on pathway assumptions, crop conditions, data sources, and system boundaries. Modeled economic impacts are not direct measurements of farm profitability. Research presented in Chinese at the 2025 Chinese Ecological Congress. An English summary is provided here; complete unpublished slides and underlying tables are not public. Read the project summary MODEL WORKFLOWS & SCENARIO TESTING 03 / Grazing-management scenarios Tools: MEMS Grazing Scheduler and related model workflows, with DayCent experience from training and project work. Tasks: management scenario input preparation, run testing, output interpretation, reproducible documentation, and carbon-accounting requirement review. Scope: these were ecosystem modeling and accounting tasks, not an independently developed ranch-profitability model. Only general work descriptions are shared; private project repositories and model input files remain restricted. Read the project summary Research materials and reproducibility Publicly shareable posters, figures, and code will be linked here after author and collaborator permissions are confirmed. The earlier synthetic demonstration dataset has been removed to distinguish teaching examples from actual research outputs.
